candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes monotonous cells with vesicular nuclei, nuclear grooves, anastomosing cords, and single-file arrangement in a myxoid stroma — features characteristic of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC). Myxoid liposarcoma typically shows lipoblasts, a delicate 'chicken-wire' vasculature, and DDIT3 (CHOP) rearrangements, none of which are described. Both are myxoid sarcomas of the thigh but represent incompatible subtypes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Myxoid liposarcoma is a distinct myxoid sarcoma subtype with different histogenesis, cytology, and molecular profile from extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma

case_quality_flags: Cytological description (nuclear grooves, anastomosing cords, single-file pattern, monotonous cells in myxoid stroma) strongly supports EMC over myxoid liposarcoma
Long clinical history (10 years) is consistent with the indolent growth pattern of EMC
